summary: Mark Roussin opens his November playbook on rotation beneath a gloomy surface: headline tech volatility, AI-spending ROI doubts, stubborn inflation and rate uncertainty mask improving market participation and sectors moving higher. He then names five November buys. MercadoLibre, down nearly 20% year to date after Brazil's election shock, is a reiterated BUY: he owns it, last bought in May/June, expects 40%+ EPS growth in each of the next two years at a 29x multiple, and cites an analyst average target of $2,160, about 30% upside. Boeing is his first explicit BUY, a long-term cash-flow turnaround rather than a next-month trade, with a record backlog and free cash flow turning positive; he owns it. Sterling Infrastructure is a reiterated BUY on a dynamite third quarter, revenue up 127%, adjusted EPS up 118%, e-infrastructure revenue up 212% and a backlog near $4B, with a recent $500 target (about 35% upside) against an analyst average of $777 he calls optimistic. Broadcom is a reiterated BUY, down nearly 15% despite record results, with his 25x math implying about $500 (about 50% upside). Nvidia is a reiterated BUY he calls the easiest buy in the market, near $100B cash versus $38B debt at a 13x forward P/E, with an analyst target near $340 (over 60% upside). No flips.
